story_type: NASA photographer rides the back seat of a T-38 in an astronaut formation over the Moon rocket
hook: Four jets, one Moon rocket, and a camera in the back seat.
narration: Four NASA jets flew in formation right over a Moon rocket on its pad.
In the back seat of one sat NASA photographer Josh Valcarcel, with cameras mounted all around him.
His pilots were NASA astronauts, headed for the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Astronauts fly these T-38 trainer jets to keep their flying skills sharp between missions.
The other jets held their places just off the wingtips the whole way.
outcome: The formation passed over Artemis I on its launch pad, then landed with every camera still rolling.
title: T-38 formation over a Moon rocket
question_comment: Would you take the back seat on this flight if NASA offered?

facts.claim: NASA photographer Josh Valcarcel rode with NASA astronauts in a T-38 to Kennedy to see Artemis I on the pad
facts.source_quote: NASA photographer Josh Valcarcel takes you behind-the-scenes to show his perspective riding with NASA astronauts to NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida to check out Artemis I on the launch pad.

facts.claim: He flew in the back seat of a NASA T-38
facts.source_quote: Ever wondered what it's like to fly backseat in a NASA T-38?

description:
NASA photographer Josh Valcarcel rides the back seat of a NASA T-38 with NASA astronauts to the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, flying past Artemis I on the launch pad in 2022.
